The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Every year we select new junior professionals into the Canonical Kernel Team, to work on the Linux kernel for Ubuntu. If you’ve enjoyed operating systems in your coursework or current role, you are confident in your ability to write high quality C and possibly Rust, and are ready to take the plunge and see how it all works, then this would be a great place to pursue your next career stage. We are a global team working to ship the world's most widely used Linux kernel, across the very latest silicon and cloud, where you can apply and grow your software engineering skills.

The Canonical Kernel Team builds and maintains all supported Ubuntu Linux kernels for a variety of platforms and architectures from small embedded devices to standard desktop/server systems to large-scale cloud environments. In your first year you will tackle serious initiatives, which include but are not limited to:

  • Optimized solutions for key Silicon and Cloud partner platforms
  • Developer platforms such as Raspberry Pi and RISC-V
  • Enabling Ubuntu on a wide range of embedded systems
  • Security hardening and exploit mitigation
  • Third-party driver integration and distribution, such as graphics
  • Expanded driver support for bleeding-edge PC platforms

We select candidates that are recent university graduates or early career professionals who are enthusiastic to develop kernel-level software in multiple areas including security updates, patching, and testing. The successful candidate will have a background in software engineering, be motivated to work in a distributed team and willing and able to travel globally twice a year for company engineering events.

These are full-time positions available to prospective or recently graduated students.

Location: We have home-based Kernel Teams in every timezone.

  • Collaborate regularly and proactively with a globally distributed team
  • Learn from senior mentors to demystify the inner workings of the Linux kernel and how it is distributed
  • Work closely with external silicon, cloud, or hardware manufacturer delivery teams on bleeding-edge platforms
  • Diagnose and resolve issues in the kernel reported by customers, the community, and discovered by your own rigorous testing
  • Take personal responsibility for the delivery of various flavors of the Ubuntu Linux kernel
  • Improve tooling and automation for delivery and test of Ubuntu Linux kernels
  • Submit, review, and apply kernel patches, working with both internal and external upstream maintainers

What we are looking for in you

  • Professional manner with colleagues, business partners, and the open-source community
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English, both written and verbal
  • Programming experience in C and/or Rust
  • Familiarity with version control practices, ideally with git
  • Understanding of operating system kernel fundamentals
  • Ability to travel twice a year for company events of up to two weeks length

Nice-to-have skills

  • Interest and experience in Rust
  • Python and Bash scripting ability
  • Prior experience with Ubuntu/Debian/Snap packaging
  • Demonstrated experience with kernel patching and debugging
  • Strong grasp of device drivers, BSP’s, and other low level system engineering

raw.description:
Our Company

Abilis Health Plan

Overview

The Chief Medical Officer (CMO) provides executive clinical leadership for Abilis Health’s Institutional Special Needs Plan (I-SNP) and Institutional-Equivalent Special Needs Plan (IE-SNP) Medicare Advantage products. The CMO is responsible for the strategic direction and oversight of clinical programs including utilization management, clinical operations, quality, population health, and pharmacy operations to ensure safe, effective, and financially responsible care for members in long term care settings. The CMO serves as the senior physician executive, partnering with the CEO and leadership team to drive clinical performance, regulatory compliance, and an integrated model of care for high-acuity, medically complex populations.

Responsibilities

  • Provide overall clinical leadership for the plans products, including development and execution of the clinical strategy aligned with organizational goals.
  • Oversee utilization management, including prior authorization criteria, medical necessity determinations, concurrent review, and appeals, ensuring evidence based and compliant decision making.
  • Lead clinical operations, including care management, transitional care, and interdisciplinary team processes to improve outcomes and reduce preventable utilization.
  • Oversight and collaboration with the VP of Quality to develop the Stars strategy, quality improvement initiatives, clinical guidelines, performance monitoring, Model of Care and corrective action plans.
  • Provide clinical oversight of pharmacy strategy, including formulary design input, medication management programs, appropriate use initiatives, and coordination with Part D partners.
  • Review and interpret clinical, utilization, and quality data to identify trends, risk areas, and opportunities for improvement; implement interventions and track impact.
  • Collaborate with network physicians, facility medical directors, advanced practice clinicians, and facility leadership to support consistent, high quality care delivery.
  • Partner with compliance and regulatory teams to ensure adherence to CMS regulations, audit readiness, and timely response to regulatory changes.
  • Participate as a key member of the executive leadership team in strategic planning, product design, benefit strategy, and growth initiatives.
  • Represent the health plan with regulators, external partners, and professional organizations as the senior clinical spokesperson.

Qualifications

  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) required.
  • Completion of an accredited residency program and board certification in an appropriate specialty.
  • Minimum of 7–10 years of clinical practice experience, with at least 3–5 years in health plan, managed care, or population health leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated experience leading utilization management, quality improvement, and care management functions in a payer, integrated delivery system, or large group practice.
  • Experience with Medicare Advantage, Special Needs Plans, or comparable government programs strongly preferred.
  • Prior leadership experience working with long term care, nursing facilities, assisted living, or other institutional/complex geriatric populations preferred.
  • Active, unrestricted medical license in at least one state in which the plan operates; eligibility for additional state licensure as needed. (KY, TN)
  • Current board certification in an appropriate medical specialty.
  • Ability to maintain all licenses, certifications, and professional memberships required by the organization and applicable regulatory bodies.
  • In depth knowledge of Medicare Advantage, Special Needs Plans (I-SNP/IE-SNP), CMS regulations, and related clinical and compliance requirements.
  • Strong understanding of utilization management, quality measurement (including Stars and HEDIS), care management models, and pharmacy management in a managed care environment.
  • Proven leadership skills, including ability to lead and influence physicians and multidisciplinary teams, drive accountability, and manage change.
  • Excellent analytical skills with the ability to interpret clinical, financial, and operational data and translate insights into actionable strategies.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex clinical and regulatory concepts to clinical and nonclinical stakeholders, executives, boards, and external partners.
  • Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships with providers, facilities, and community partners in a highly regulated, performance driven environment.
  • Strategic, systems level thinker with the ability to balance clinical quality, member experience, regulatory requirements, and financial stewardship.
  • High integrity, sound clinical judgment, and commitment to ethical decision making and member centered care.

About our Line of Business

Abilis Health Plan, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, is a Medicare Advantage Plan covering all the benefits of Original Medicare (Parts A and B) with prescription drug coverage (Part D). The Abilis Health Plan is a unique plan allowing members to enroll year-round. The plan focuses on members who meet residential requirements in participating nursing facilities. An interdisciplinary team of clinicians and innovative services allow us to meet each member’s clinical needs and provide preventive, coordinated, and quality healthcare. With a dedicated nurse practitioner leading a personalized care plan, we strive to improve the health of the communities in which we serve. For more information, please visit www.abilishealth.com. Follow us on LinkedIn.

JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way.

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.

The MTS Service Delivery Manager is the operational and regional execution leader for a dedicated client account, responsible for day-to-day service delivery, performance accountability, and quality assurance across all MTS operations in their region. Reporting to the Account Leader, you own accountability for KPI performance, staffing optimization, quality standards, and regional client satisfaction. You are the primary operational point of contact for client facility managers—the face of MTS in your region. You'll serve as the trusted advisor on all operational matters, respond directly to facility manager needs, and coordinate across Operations Managers to ensure consistent execution, SLA compliance, and continuous improvement.

This is an operationally intense, client-facing role grounded in execution rigor and accountability. You'll move between strategic priorities (staffing planning, KPI corrective action, capability gaps) and tactical execution (quality audits, schedule optimization, issue escalation and resolution). Success requires the ability to build strong client relationships, drive accountability across your region without direct hiring authority (by design—keeping your focus on execution and client delivery, not hiring logistics), collaborate effectively with Operations Managers, anticipate client needs, and maintain discipline around cost, quality, and safety standards.

What sets this role apart is the direct client visibility and trust. You translate account strategy into consistent, reliable service delivery—ensuring every technician, every shift, and every work order reflects MTS's commitment to technical excellence and operational reliability, and ensuring the client knows that MTS is operationally responsive and committed to their success.

What your day-to-day will look like:

Client Relationship & Regional Operations

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with client facility managers; serve as their trusted operational advisor and primary point of contact for all MTS matters in your region

  • Respond directly to facility manager requests, escalations, and operational questions; ensure every interaction reflects MTS's commitment to responsiveness and reliability

  • Communicate regularly with facility managers on regional performance, staffing plans, and operational changes; gather feedback and address concerns proactively

  • Monitor SLA performance and KPI execution across your region; identify at-risk metrics and escalate to the Account Leader when corrective actions are not resolved within pre-defined time frames

  • Monitor account-level KPIs including fee-at-risk metrics; develop regional corrective action plans in collaboration with the Account Leader

  • Act as the primary escalation point for your region; support resolution of scheduling conflicts and technical issues in conjunction with Operations Managers

  • Monitor daily work order activity and respond when issues arise; resolve scheduling or operational barriers that impact SLA or client satisfaction

  • Coordinate with Operations Managers across your region to drive action on operational priorities, staffing adjustments, and quality improvements

Staffing & Operational Planning

  • Conduct ongoing analysis of MTS staffing levels, hours allocation, and skill mix for your region; provide direct input to Operations Managers on staffing needs and coverage requirements

  • Plan and coordinate staffing requirements related to client store openings and closings; ensure adequate coverage and skill mix for new locations

  • Ensure client facility information (store openings, closings, equipment changes, facility modifications) is captured and communicated to Operations Managers and field teams to inform staffing and service planning

  • Manage schedule monitoring for SLA risk; work with Operations Managers to adjust coverage and prioritization as required

Quality & Performance Accountability

  • Conduct regular quality audits at client facilities to ensure MTS service standards meet or exceed client facility manager expectations; monitor and review quality audit results and safety inspection findings conducted by Operations Managers.

  • Own accountability for quality standards and compliance in your region; establish audit protocols, identify trends, and drive corrective action

  • Provide direct feedback to Operations Managers on performance, execution gaps, quality findings, and opportunities for improvement

  • Ensure all MTS staff in your region understand quality and safety expectations; model accountability and continuous improvement

Capability Management & Field Readiness

  • Receive basic Corrigo training; audit skills assignments in Corrigo to ensure technicians are properly certified and trained for assigned work

  • Ensure client-specific training completion is tracked and current; maintain working knowledge of critical client equipment and systems relevant to your region

  • Support training delivery and skills validation; work with Operations Managers to address competency gaps and ensure field team readiness

Collaboration & Cross-Functional Alignment

raw.title: Engineering Manager - Ubuntu Desktop Apps
raw.excerpt: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets.
raw.description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

Our Ubuntu Engineering teams build the operating system platform used by millions of developers, enterprises, device makers, cloud providers, and open source communities worldwide.

Location: We have remote roles open in every time zone.

About the team

The Ubuntu Foundations Package Management team, as part of the broader Ubuntu Foundations organisation, develops and maintains the software management infrastructure that underpins every Ubuntu system.

The team owns technologies at the heart of Ubuntu's software, driver, firmware, and upgrade experience, including APT, dpkg, firmware management, and driver management.

Its mission is to provide the technologies that enable Ubuntu systems to be installed, maintained, updated, upgraded, and managed throughout their lifecycle. The team balances innovation with the stability and reliability expected from one of the world's most widely used Linux distributions.

The team works across the full engineering lifecycle, from roadmap definition and architecture through implementation, testing, release engineering, and upstream collaboration, ensuring the continued evolution of the technologies that manage software, drivers, firmware, and upgrades across Ubuntu systems.

The Role

We are looking for a Software Engineering Manager to lead the Ubuntu Foundations Package Management team.

This is a technical leadership role combining people management with active engineering involvement. You will lead a team of experienced engineers responsible for the package management and system lifecycle technologies that underpin Ubuntu. Working closely with stakeholders across Ubuntu Engineering, you will define technical direction, grow engineering talent, build strong cross-team partnerships, and ensure the continued evolution of Ubuntu's software, driver, firmware, and upgrade experience.

You will report to the Ubuntu Foundations Engineering director and collaborate closely with other Ubuntu Engineering teams, including Desktop, Server, Security, Release Engineering, Launchpad, Debcrafters, OEM, and Product.

What You’ll Do

Technical Leadership

  • Define the technical vision and roadmap for Ubuntu's package management and system lifecycle platform
  • Participate in design reviews and key technical decisions affecting software management and system lifecycle technologies across the Ubuntu ecosystem
  • Promote high standards for performance, reliability, security, and maintainability

Team Leadership

  • Lead and support a team of engineers responsible for key Ubuntu platform technologies.
  • Mentor and grow engineers, helping them expand their technical leadership, ownership, and organizational impact
  • Foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement

Delivery and Engineering Excellence

  • Plan and deliver improvements across multiple Ubuntu release cycles
  • Balance innovation with stability, compatibility, and long-term maintainability
  • Improve test automation, release quality, and operational reliability

Collaboration and Community

  • Build strong partnerships across Ubuntu Engineering, including Release Engineering, Launchpad, Desktop, Server, Security, OEM, and Product teams
  • Collaborate with Debian, upstream projects, and the Ubuntu open source community

What We Are Looking For

Required

  • An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
  • Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or STEM, or a compelling narrative about your alternative path
  • Strong background in software engineering and system design
  • Experience leading engineering teams, including people management, coaching, and performance development
  • Experience developing or operating Linux distribution technologies, package management systems, or software distribution infrastructure
  • Strong understanding of systems software and operating system architecture
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work effectively in a globally distributed engineering team
  • Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with package repositories, archives, or release engineering processes
  • Experience contributing to Debian, Ubuntu, or other open source infrastructure projects
  • Performance, reliability, or security engineering experience

We know that strong candidates may not meet every qualification. If you are excited by this role and our mission, we encourage you to apply.

What Success Looks Like

First 3 Months

  • Build strong relationships with the team and stakeholders across Ubuntu Engineering
  • Gain a deep understanding of Ubuntu package management, update flows, archive interactions, and release processes
  • Identify key improvement opportunities in reliability, test coverage, engineering processes, and product quality

First 6 to 12 Months

  • Establish strong partnerships with stakeholders across Ubuntu Engineering, including Release Engineering, Launchpad, Desktop, Server, Security, OEM, and Product
  • Grow the team and raise the overall level of engineering excellence, ownership, and technical leadership
  • Improve roadmap clarity, planning, and execution across the team's portfolio
  • Deliver meaningful improvements to Ubuntu's package management and system lifecycle platform

What we offer you

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

Career Category

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Marketing Senior Manager, UPLIZNA gMG Medical Marketing

Live

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. The Senior Manager, Neurology Medical Marketing - Opinion Leader Engagement & Peer-to-Peer (P2P) will lead the U.S. Neurology opinion leader (OL) engagement and P2P strategy, UPLIZNA Speaker Bureau, and marketing-led HCP education and engagement portfolio across gMG and NMOSD. Reporting to the Neuro Medical Marketing Lead, this individual will translate franchise and indication priorities into an integrated external engagement model that strengthens strategic relationships, customer confidence, brand differentiation, and high-quality field execution.

This role has end-to-end accountability for marketing-led OL engagement and P2P, including OL mapping and engagement planning, speaker programs, Peer Discussion Groups, industry therapeutic updates (ITUs), product theaters, symposia, speaker development, P2P content, and agency/vendor delivery. The Senior Manager will lead and develop direct reports who pull through assigned workstreams and partner closely with HCP Marketing, Medical Affairs, Field Medical, Sales, TLLs, Training, Regulatory, Legal, Market Access, Global, Professional Marketing, and other cross-functional colleagues. Advisory boards and other primary insight-generation forums are led by the Insights & Congress Strategy organization; this role translates those learnings into engagement plans.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Opinion Leader Engagement and P2P Strategy

  • Set and evolve the U.S. Neurology OL engagement and P2P strategy across gMG and NMOSD, aligning marketing-led HCP education and engagement with franchise priorities, customer needs, scientific developments, competitive dynamics, and lifecycle objectives.

  • Own OL mapping, segmentation, and engagement planning for established and emerging OLs, in partnership with Medical Affairs, Field Medical, TLLs, and HCP Marketing.

  • Establish clear engagement objectives, audience segmentation, deployment plans, and success measures for the portfolio; ensure each activity is appropriately aligned to customer, indication, and business needs.

  • Lead annual and in-year P2P and OL engagement planning, including program volume, geographic deployment, investment allocation, and contingency planning across both indications.

Own and Evolve the UPLIZNA Speaker Bureau and P2P Portfolio

  • Own the strategy, design, and execution of the UPLIZNA Speaker Bureau, including bureau composition, speaker segmentation, recruitment, onboarding, contracting coordination, activation, and ongoing optimization.

  • Own the end-to-end design and execution of marketing-led HCP education and P2P programs, including speaker programs, Peer Discussion Groups, ITUs, and other approved customer education opportunities.

  • Lead speaker training and development strategy, including curriculum design, content readiness, faculty preparation, and ongoing capability building for new and tenured speakers.

  • Partner with Sales Training and field leadership to strengthen field readiness, appropriate program pull-through, and a consistent customer experience.

Lead Opinion Leader Engagement at Congresses

  • Own all marketing-led OL-facing engagement at congresses, including ITUs, symposia, product theaters, speaker and faculty activity, and other approved OL-present programs.

raw.description:
Position Summary

The QME Deposition Associate represents the firm's clients by preparing for and personally conducting Qualified Medical Evaluator (QME) depositions in workers' compensation cases. This role is responsible for reviewing case files ahead of scheduled depositions to identify opportunities for resolution prior to deposition, preparing deposition strategy and questions, and appearing at and conducting QME depositions — both applicant-set and defense-set — to develop the record and advance the client's position. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable working independently under deadline pressure in a fast-paced workers' compensation litigation environment.

Key Responsibilities

Pre-Deposition Case Review

  • Review assigned case files in advance of each scheduled QME deposition to assess case status, medical-legal issues, and litigation posture.
  • Evaluate whether resolution (settlement, stipulation) is achievable prior to the deposition date, and discuss viable cases with the adjuster or client.
  • Communicate with attorneys, adjusters, and opposing counsel to explore early resolution options and confirm whether a deposition can be avoided, continued, or must proceed.
  • Document case review findings and resolution recommendations in the case management system.

Deposition Preparation

  • Review the case file in depth prior to the QME deposition, including claim history, prior medical treatment records, and the QME/AME report(s), to identify key factual and medical issues.
  • Analyze the QME report(s) for internal inconsistencies, gaps, causation issues, apportionment concerns, or areas that need clarification through testimony.
  • Identify disputed issues (e.g., AOE/COE, body parts, permanent disability, need for further treatment, apportionment) and determine what the deposition needs to establish or challenge.
  • Contact the client as needed to get an updated sense of their current medical status, ongoing symptoms, treatment, and how their case is progressing, to make sure the questions and strategy reflect where things stand.

Deposition Attendance

  • Appear at and conduct QME depositions — both applicant-set and defense-set — in person or remotely, questioning the QME and making appropriate objections on the record.
  • Take detailed notes during depositions, tracking key testimony, exhibits marked, and outstanding issues.
  • Manage exhibits and make real-time strategic decisions on the scope and direction of questioning during the deposition.
  • Coordinate post-deposition follow-up tasks.

Administrative & Case Management

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date case files, deposition logs, and status reports.
  • Communicate proactively with internal team members regarding case status, resolution opportunities, and deposition outcomes.
  • Perform other litigation duties as assigned.
  • Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree and active license to practice law in California (active member of the State Bar of California) required.
  • 1+ years of experience litigating workers' compensation cases, including taking QME/AME depositions, strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of California workers' compensation procedures, QME processes, and deposition practice (or willingness to learn quickly).
  • Prior experience as an associate attorney in a workers' compensation defense or applicant firm is a plus.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to assess case files and identify resolution opportunities.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple deposition schedules simultaneously.

  • Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and meet firm deadlines.

  • Proficiency with case management software, Microsoft Office (Word, Outlook, Excel), and e-filing/e-service systems.

  • Professional demeanor and courtroom-appropriate presence suitable for examining medical evaluators and appearing opposite opposing counsel.

Work Environment

  • Standard office environment with regular travel to QME offices, deposition sites, or virtual deposition platforms.

  • May require occasional early morning, evening, or extended hours to accommodate deposition schedules.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary of $110,000 -$130,000 and performance-based bonuses.
  • Comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, retirement plans, and unlimited paid time off (PTO).
  • Opportunities for professional development and continuing legal education (CLE).
  • A supportive work environment dedicated to teamwork, integrity, and excellence in client service.

What You'd Be Doing in This Role:

Every team at Canva builds and ships on top of infrastructure that has to be fast, reliable, and easy to work with. That's what this role is about: owning and evolving the core systems that let engineering teams across Canva talk to each other's services, route traffic safely, and build in the languages that suit their work. As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll take technical ownership of a meaningful piece of that platform and help set the direction for where it goes next.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Designing and building the core infrastructure that connects services across Canva's backend engineering org
  • Leading a major migration of how our backend services communicate, working closely with partner engineering teams & leaders
  • Driving support for more languages and frameworks so more teams can build natively on our platform
  • Owning the reliability, performance and correctness of systems that sit in the critical path for the whole engineering org
  • Mentoring engineers and helping raise the technical bar across the team

You're Probably a Match If:

  • You've built and operated infrastructure that other engineering teams depend on, ideally something in the API gateway, RPC, or service mesh space (high traffic & large-scale).
  • You're comfortable owning systems where reliability and correctness really matter, and you think in trade-offs rather than quick fixes
  • You can drive a technical direction across teams that don't report to you, and communicate it clearly to both engineers and the teams who consume what you build
  • You take genuine ownership of outcomes, and you're motivated by platform work that quietly makes everyone else's job easier
  • You've spent years owning large-scale, high-transaction production systems commercially, and ideally worked in more than one language along the way.

About the Team:

We build and run the infrastructure that lets every other engineering team at Canva move fast without worrying about the plumbing underneath them. From how services talk to each other, to how traffic is routed and secured, to giving teams the freedom to build in the language that's right for the job, our work shows up in every product built on Canva's platform.

Don't tick all the boxes? Don't worry about that - nobody does!

We’d still love to hear from you! At Canva, we know that great engineers come from a variety of backgrounds, and we value passion, curiosity, and a willingness to learn just as much as specific experience. If you're excited about this role but don’t tick every box, we encourage you to apply, you might a great fit in ways you didn’t expect!

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

Are you a MIIS student with a unique internship idea based on your area of interest and expertise? Apply to any open MIIS internship posting, upload your resume, and outline your proposal in your cover letter.

CLEAR Global is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to having a diverse team where individuals of all backgrounds collaborate and learn from one another. We believe we can be most effective with diverse experience and expertise in our team. We recruit on merit, actively seek diverse applicant pools, and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, marital or parental status, or sexual orientation, and welcome all types of diversity.

Background

CLEAR Global is a nonprofit organization helping people get vital information and be heard, whatever language they speak. As part of this mission, CLEAR Global maintains the Language Use Data Platform (LUDP), a data platform that aggregates and standardizes language and geographic data to support humanitarian and language-access initiatives globally.

As LUDP expands into additional countries and languages, CLEAR Global is piloting and refining workflows for identifying, processing, validating, and publishing multilingual datasets. This internship will support the testing and documentation of these operational processes to help ensure they are scalable, accurate, and sustainable.

Objectives

The objective of this internship is to support a pilot implementation of the “Adding a Country” workflow for LUDP. The intern will help test and document the feasibility, clarity, and timing of the process by working through real country-level language datasets and supporting data preparation, validation, and reporting activities.

The role

The MIIS Intern will support the LUDP Team in piloting workflows related to language dataset acquisition, processing, quality assurance, and publication. Working closely with CLEAR Global staff, the intern will contribute to testing operational procedures, documenting findings, identifying gaps or inefficiencies, and helping improve internal guidance and processes for future country expansion efforts.

Responsibilities

  • Support the identification and acquisition of country-level language datasets from public and institutional sources.
  • Prepare and standardize datasets for integration into the LUDP environment.
  • Assist with data cleaning, formatting, and metadata verification.
  • Run and document data processing workflows using existing tools and templates.
  • Support quality assurance and validation activities, including cross-referencing linguistic and geographic information.
  • Document workflow challenges, ambiguities, timing estimates, and process improvement recommendations.
  • Assist in drafting update reports and maintaining process documentation.
  • Collaborate with CLEAR Global staff to refine operational guidance and workflow materials.
  • Undertake other quality operations tasks as assigned.
  • Act in the best interest of the organization during the project period.

These roles and responsibilities are approximate and may change over time.

Qualifications

  • Current graduate student at the Middlebury Institute of International Studies (MIIS), preferably in Translation & Localization Management, Localization Project Management, TESOL, Language Technology, Data Analytics, or a related field.
  • Strong organizational and analytical skills.
  • Attention to detail and ability to follow structured processes.
  • Comfort working with spreadsheets and structured datasets.
  • Interest in language data, multilingual technology, humanitarian technology, or localization workflows.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • Strong written and spoken English.

Requirements

This position is very dynamic. The right person is an energetic team player who agrees with CLEAR Global’s basic beliefs and values and can work remotely while interacting regularly with the international team.

  • Self-starter;
  • Strong organizational skills;
  • Analytical thinker able to transform ideas into tangible actions;
  • Understands that communication in the right language is key to improved humanitarian response;
  • Team player, collaborative, adaptable and self-motivated;
  • Interest in acquiring translation project management experience;
  • Ability to adapt to new technologies and learn new skills quickly;
  • Attention to detail.

About CLEAR Global

CLEAR Global exists to help people get vital information, and be heard, whatever language they speak. We believe that everyone has the right to give and receive information in a language and format they understand. We work with nonprofit partners and a global community of language professionals to build local language translation capacity, and raise awareness of language barriers. Our network of over 200,000 community members translate millions of words of life-saving and life-changing information a year.

Core values

CLEAR Global employees and volunteers are people who believe passionately about the value of this work and take personal responsibility for achieving the mission. CLEAR Global’s mission and organizational spirit embody the core values established in its strategic framework:

  • Excellence: As the leading voice for communicating humanitarian information in the right language, CLEAR Global is a leader in the translation industry and in the non-profit sector.
  • Integrity: CLEAR Global believes that every person, whether it’s the people who we serve, our volunteers or our staff, has value, deserves respect and has inherent dignity.
  • Empowerment: CLEAR Global believes in using language to empower people around the world to control their own development and destiny.
  • Innovation: CLEAR Global recognizes and celebrates the power of innovation to address humanitarian and crisis issues around the world.
  • Sustainability: CLEAR Global recognizes that meeting our mission necessitates establishment and maintenance of a solid financial and organizational infrastructure.
  • Tolerance: Our staff and volunteers are highly knowledgeable and skilled; value each other, our partner and our recipients; create a supportive work environment; and conduct themselves professionally at all times.

CLEAR Global may re-advertise the vacancy, cancel the recruitment, offer an appointment with a modified job description or for a different duration at its discretion.

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

Nebius is experiencing continuous business growth, particularly in fixed asset transactions. To support this expansion while maintaining strong financial controls, operational efficiency, and compliance standards, we are strengthening our finance team.

We are looking for an experienced Fixed Assets Accountant who will take ownership of fixed asset accounting processes, support month-end close activities, and contribute to process optimization and automation initiatives. In this role, you will partner closely with finance, procurement, operational and logistic teams to ensure accurate financial reporting, strong internal controls, and scalable accounting processes in a fast-growing international environment.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Own and maintain the fixed asset register, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with internal policies, SOX requirements, and US GAAP.
  • Review and process fixed asset acquisitions, disposals, transfers, depreciation, and other related transactions in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual fixed asset close activities, including reconciliations, journal entries, and reporting.
  • Coordinate and support fixed asset stock counts and related control procedures across business units.
  • Partner with procurement, FP&A, and operational teams to improve purchasing and capitalization processes in line with business growth plans.
  • Support internal and external audits by preparing documentation, responding to audit requests, and ensuring compliance with control requirements.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvements, automation, and optimization within fixed asset accounting workflows.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional finance and systems teams to enhance integrations and reporting capabilities across platforms such as NetSuite and BlackLine.
  • Contribute to the development and documentation of accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls.

We expect you to have:

  • 6+ years of accounting experience, including substantial hands-on experience in fixed assets accounting.
  • Strong understanding of US GAAP, fixed asset accounting principles, and SOX/internal control frameworks.
  • Experience working with ERP systems, preferably NetSuite or similar financial platforms.
  • Proven ability to manage high transaction volumes and meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong analytical, reconciliation, and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail.
  • Advanced Excel skills and experience working with financial reporting and reconciliation tools.
  • Ability to work independently, take ownership of processes, and drive improvements proactively.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills in an international environment.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience with process automation, finance transformation, or ERP/system integrations.
  • Previous experience in a multinational, high-growth, or technology-driven company.
  • Experience with BlackLine or similar reconciliation and close management tools.
  • Big4 background or external audit experience.
  • Experience supporting SOX compliance in a public-company environment.

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.

Base Compensation Range
$110,000—$140,000 USD

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

NeoGenomics has an opening for a Commercial Strategic Initiatives and AI Integration Manager who wants to continue to learn in order to allow our company to grow. The ideal candidate will be located remotely within the United States.

Now that you know what we're looking for in talent, let us tell you why you'd want to work at NeoGenomics:

As an employer, we promise to provide you with a purpose driven mission in which you have the opportunity to save lives by improving patient care through the exceptional work you perform. Together, we will become the world's leading cancer reference laboratory.

Position Summary

The Commercial Strategic Initiatives and AI Integration Manager is responsible for defining and advancing the artificial intelligence (AI) strategy for the NeoGenomics Commercial organization, spanning both current state assessment and future state direction. This role establishes where and how AI creates measurable commercial advantage, prioritizes investment against the organization's growth objectives, and ensures that efforts are connected across Commercial functions rather than pursued in isolation.

The role works cross-functionally with Commercial leadership, Digital Technology Solutions (DTS), Legal, and Compliance to ensure alignment between commercial ambition, technical feasibility, and the obligations that come with operating in a regulated healthcare environment. It also serves as the Commercial organization's point of contact for AI across NeoGenomics, representing Commercial in enterprise AI initiatives and governance.

This role requires a strategic thinker with direct AI or advanced analytics experience and the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority to achieve measurable outcomes.

Core Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain a clear assessment of AI adoption across the Commercial organization, including tools in use, pilots underway, spend, capability gaps, and duplicated effort.
  • Define the multi-year AI strategy for Commercial, including a prioritized roadmap, sequencing, and a defensible position on what the organization builds, buys, or defers.
  • Serve as the connection point for AI across Commercial functions, ensuring each function has a clear path to applying AI against its own priorities and that the organization learns from every effort.
  • Serve as the Commercial point of contact for AI across NeoGenomics, representing Commercial priorities, requirements, and constraints in enterprise discussions and bringing enterprise developments back into Commercial planning.
  • Represent Commercial on enterprise project and governance teams aligned to AI initiatives, ensuring Commercial needs are reflected in decisions on tooling, data, and policy.
  • Establish consistent criteria for evaluating AI opportunities, size the value, and bring recommendations to the Commercial Leadership Team.
  • Lead a focused set of proof-of-concept initiatives that validate the strategy in practice, then transition successful efforts to the owning function with a plan for scale.
  • Partner with Commercial Training to build AI fluency across the Commercial organization and drive at-scale adoption.
  • Partner with DTS, Legal, and Compliance to ensure the Commercial approach to AI meets company standards for data governance, privacy, and protected health information (PHI).
  • Monitor the vendor landscape, competitor activity, and the evolving regulatory environment as it affects commercial use of AI in diagnostics and translate those developments into recommendations for senior leadership.
  • Communicate strategy, progress, and performance metrics to senior leadership and key stakeholders.
  • Establish and execute the AI strategy that advances the growth objectives of the NeoGenomics Commercial organization.
  • Represent the Commercial organization in enterprise AI initiatives and governance.
  • Lead additional projects and strategic initiatives assigned by the Senior Director, Commercial Strategy.

Experience, Education and Qualifications

  • Master's Degree preferred.
  • 8+ years of experience in strategy, commercial operations, technology strategy, consulting, or a related field.
  • 4+ years of experience leading cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.
  • Direct experience with AI or advanced analytics, including a working understanding of current capabilities and their limitations.
  • Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to translate an ambiguous and fast-moving environment into a clear plan with explicit trade-offs.

Note: This is a strategic job posting to network for future anticipated opportunities as we continue to grow. While this may not be an immediate need, we would love the opportunity to connect with you.

ICF Next brings together strategy, creativity, data, and technology to solve complex challenges and move people when it matters most.

We work with organizations tackling some of today's most important issues—from public health and energy to climate, resilience, and economic opportunity. Our work isn't simply about communication. It's about helping people understand, make informed decisions, build confidence, and take meaningful action.

We create integrated campaigns and experiences that connect with people wherever they are, building ideas that work seamlessly across channels and endure across every touchpoint. Whether we're launching a national behavior-change campaign, helping communities navigate change, or strengthening trust, we believe the best creative work combines insight, strategy, and exceptional craft to create measurable impact.

The Role

We are looking for a Group Creative Director who can lead important work, build exceptional teams, and create the conditions for ambitious ideas to thrive.

This role sits at the heart of Creative. The Group Creative Director is responsible for the quality, direction, and creative sensibility of a significant portfolio of work, as well as the teams responsible for creating it. This person should be able to see the big picture without losing sight of the idea, the craft, or the audience. They should know when to push, when to protect, and when to simplify.

Much of the work will address some of the most consequential issues facing people and communities, including public health, public safety, education, energy, environmental sustainability, and other mission-driven challenges. These are often complex issues involving diverse audiences, competing priorities, deeply held beliefs, and decisions with meaningful consequences.

The right experience, however, can come from anywhere truly great integrated creative work gets made. Consumer. Healthcare. Technology. Culture. We are looking for someone who understands not just how creativity can attract attention, but how the right idea can make complex information human, connect with people, shift perception, build confidence, and move audiences to act.

The strongest candidates will have a body of work that demonstrates original thinking, exceptional creative judgment, and consistently high standards of craft. Industry recognition and award-winning work are valued, but what matters most is evidence of ideas that were distinctive, beautifully made, strategically sound, and effective.

What You Will Do:

  • Lead the creative direction, quality, and vision of a significant portfolio of clients, integrated campaigns, and multidisciplinary creative teams.
  • Develop breakthrough integrated campaigns that translate strategy, audience insight, behavioral understanding, and cultural context into ideas that connect with people and create measurable impact.
  • Lead creative development from brief through production, ensuring every execution reflects the strength of the original idea and the highest standards of craft.
  • Build, mentor, and inspire Creative Directors, Associate Creative Directors, writers, art directors, designers, and other creative specialists, creating an environment where ambitious ideas and exceptional people can thrive.
  • Partner closely with strategy, research, behavioral science, media, production, communications, experience design, and technology teams to deliver seamless integrated campaigns across every channel.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior clients and stakeholders, confidently presenting ambitious creative thinking and guiding complex decision-making while protecting the integrity of the work.
  • Lead major productions across film, photography, digital, social, experiential, and emerging platforms, ensuring creative excellence from concept to final delivery.
  • Play a significant leadership role in new business, pitches, and agency growth by helping shape winning strategies, creative platforms, and client relationships.
  • Champion creative excellence while ensuring work meets the highest standards of accessibility, inclusivity, clarity, effectiveness, and measurable performance.
  • Help shape the creative culture, standards, capabilities, and long-term reputation of ICF Next.

What Makes This Role Different

The Group Creative Director defines the creative standard for a significant portfolio of work. They don't simply oversee campaigns—they build teams, shape creative culture, strengthen client relationships, and create the conditions for exceptional ideas to thrive.

They move comfortably between the biggest strategic challenge and the smallest creative detail, knowing when to challenge an idea, when to simplify it, and when to protect it. They understand that exceptional creative work is built by exceptional creative teams and invest in both with equal commitment.

What We Are Looking For:

Basic Qualifications

  • 15+ years of agency or equivalent creative experience, including deep experience leading integrated campaigns and multidisciplinary creative teams.
  • An exceptional portfolio demonstrating original conceptual thinking, creative leadership, and a consistent ability to produce strategically smart, beautifully crafted work that delivers measurable results.

Professional Skills

  • A proven track record of building, mentoring, and leading high-performing creative teams while establishing a clear creative vision across a significant portfolio of work.
  • Extensive experience developing integrated campaigns across video, digital, social, experiential, print, out-of-home, web, emerging platforms, and connected customer experiences.
  • Exceptional creative judgment and the ability to recognize, shape, challenge, and protect powerful ideas from concept through execution.
  • Deep understanding of how strategy, audience insight, behavioral science, storytelling, design, technology, and craft come together to create work that moves people.
  • Experience translating complex, technical, scientific, regulated, or sensitive subject matter into compelling creative communications that people genuinely engage with.
  • Confidence presenting ambitious creative thinking to senior executives, clients, and diverse stakeholder groups while building trust and creative momentum.
  • Experience developing campaigns addressing public health, public safety, education, energy, environmental sustainability, climate, or other complex mission-driven challenges is highly valued. Public-sector experience is welcome but not required.
  • Industry recognition is valued, but what matters most is a body of work that demonstrates originality, exceptional craft, strategic thinking, and measurable impact.

raw.description:
Clearance

Public Trust

Overview

Ardent Eagle Solutions (AES) is seeking Records Management Specialists to support a competitive federal contracting opportunity with the U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), Economic Development Administration (EDA).

The Records Management Specialist will support the assessment, modernization, and ongoing execution of EDA's Records Management Program. Working alongside senior records management personnel and Government stakeholders, this position will assist with records inventories, audits, electronic records management, document control, disposition activities, administrative procedures, program documentation, and records management training and sustainment efforts.

Background

EDA requires contractor support to strengthen and standardize records management practices across its Headquarters and six regional offices. The program is intended to improve records inventories and disposition processes, digital and email records controls, process documentation, training, and the overall consistency and sustainability of EDA's Records Management Program.

The work will support a broader effort to establish practical, repeatable records management processes and transfer usable tools and resources to Government personnel.

Responsibilities

The Records Management Specialist is expected to:

  • Support Senior Records Managers in assessing, redesigning, and executing EDA's Records Management Program.
  • Assist with the analysis, development, and review of administrative operating procedures.
  • Support records management activities, management plans, reports, and program documentation.
  • Participate in records inventories, audits, and reconciliations.
  • Identify and document records series, owners, formats, volumes, locations, restrictions, and applicable records schedules.
  • Coordinate and track document requests in accordance with applicable NARA and Federal Records Center guidance.
  • Support classification reviews, as required.
  • Respond to customer requests for records, documents, or records management assistance.
  • Digitize analog records into electronic formats in accordance with applicable NARA standards.
  • Support preparation of expired records for authorized destruction or other disposition.
  • Perform records receipt, storage, indexing, and inventory activities.
  • Conduct quality control reviews of records and box contents.
  • Perform inventory reconciliations and assist with identifying discrepancies or corrective actions.
  • Support digital and electronic records activities involving email, electronic messages, shared drives, SharePoint, and other repositories.
  • Assist in developing SOPs, desk guides, checklists, training materials, and other records management resources.
  • Coordinate schedules for deliverables, reviews, briefings, and other program activities.
  • Assist with progress reporting, transition activities, and knowledge transfer.
  • Collaborate with geographically dispersed Government and contractor personnel to support consistent records management practices across EDA.

Qualifications

Approximately 4 or more years of related professional experience in records management, document management, information management, information governance, administrative records support, or a closely related field.

  • Experience working with NARA records retention policies, schedules, or records management requirements.
  • Experience supporting records inventories, file plans, records disposition, document control, indexing, digitization, or records reconciliation activities.
  • Familiarity with electronic records and common digital repositories, such as shared drives, SharePoint, email systems, or comparable platforms.
  • Ability to organize, track, review, and reconcile large volumes of records or information accurately.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality control.
  • Ability to interpret established policies and procedures and apply them consistently.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with senior records management personnel, Government stakeholders, and geographically dispersed teams.
  • Prior federal records management or federal contracting experience is preferred.

Education

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.

Location and Work Hours

This position is expected to be primarily remote and may be performed from locations throughout the United States, subject to final contract requirements and Government approval.

Although this requisition may be advertised using Washington, D.C. as the posting location, candidates are not expected to reside in the Washington metropolitan area solely because of the posting location.

The position will support EDA Headquarters and/or one or more regional offices located in Philadelphia, Atlanta, Chicago, Austin, Denver, and Seattle. Current contract documentation anticipates primarily remote performance with onsite support when appropriately authorized.

Normal work hours are expected to be Monday through Friday during standard business hours, excluding Federal holidays and Government-directed closures.

Travel

Approximately 10% travel is anticipated based on current planning assumptions. Travel may include authorized visits to EDA Headquarters or regional offices to support inventories, assessments, meetings, records activities, training, or other program requirements.

Compensation

Anticipated Salary Range: $60,000- $70,000 annually

This position is being recruited in support of a competitive federal contracting opportunity, and AES is continuing to develop its staffing, labor category, and compensation strategy. Because this position is expected to support a primarily remote workforce and qualified candidates may reside in different geographic markets throughout the United States, compensation expectations may vary considerably by location.

Final compensation will consider factors including geographic market, relevant experience, education, specialized records management expertise, applicable labor category requirements, and contractual and business considerations.

AES welcomes open and collaborative compensation discussions with interested candidates as we evaluate the market and develop an accurate and competitive compensation strategy for this opportunity. The range above represents our current anticipated range and is not a guarantee of a specific salary or compensation level.

Benefits and EEO

At Ardent Eagle Solutions, we offer a comprehensive benefits package to our employees and their families:

  • Medical/Dental/Vision Coverage
  • Matching 401(k) Plan
  • Continuing Education Assistance
  • Paid Time Off

This job description is intended to describe the general scope of work and level of work that is needed to perform while on task with Ardent Eagle Solutions. Other duties may be assigned. Selected candidates may undergo a government security investigation and must fulfill eligibility criteria for accessing classified information. US citizenship may be a prerequisite for certain roles.

Ardent Eagle Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to disability or protected veteran status.

﻿

We are seeking a highly experienced and results-oriented Senior Director of Sales to lead our client’s global sales strategy within the Money Transfer Operator (MTO) and Payment Service Provider (PSP) sectors.   • Minimum of 10 years of progressive sales leadership experience, with a significant focus on the Money Transfer Operator (MTO) and/or Payment Service Provider (PSP) sectors.

We light up the world, literally. Customers have chosen Sunco to provide millions of LED lights and trust us for our exceptional customer service, eco-conscious product expertise, and unmatched value.

About the role

We’re looking for a talented Video Editor to join Sunco’s Marketing team and support the growth of our video content pipeline. This role will focus on editing both short-form and long-form videos for ads, social media, tutorials, and brand storytelling.

You’ll collaborate closely with content managers, writers, designers, and videographers to bring video concepts to life while maintaining Sunco’s brand standards and performance goals.

What you'll do

  • Collaborate with content managers, writers, designers, and videographers to develop video concepts, edit plans, and basic storyboards.
  • Edit short-form and long-form videos for ads, promotions, tutorials, and brand storytelling using Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, or similar tools.
  • Create platform-native edits and variations for Amazon, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Vimeo, and other channels—optimizing for format, length, hooks, and calls to action.
  • Ensure consistency in branding, messaging, tone, and visual style across all video content.
  • Add graphics, subtitles, simple motion design, and basic animations to improve clarity and engagement.
  • Perform basic color correction and audio cleanup, including music, sound effects, and voice balancing, while following licensing and brand guidelines.
  • Optimize video files, thumbnails, titles, and metadata for SEO and discoverability.
  • Stay up to date on industry trends, creator best practices, and competitor content, and suggest new formats or creative tests.
  • Organize and maintain video assets, project files, and exports for efficient collaboration and reuse.
  • Incorporate feedback from stakeholders and partner teams while maintaining quality and timelines.
  • Manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously, communicating clearly about progress and risks.
  • Partner with internal and external videographers or agencies when needed, providing clear briefs and edit requirements.
  • Work regular hours that substantially overlap with 9:00 am – 5:00 pm Pacific Time and attend scheduled meetings.
  • Support other video and content-related tasks as needed.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in film production or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Proven experience as a video editor with a strong portfolio or showreel demonstrating end-to-end edits for digital channels, especially advertising.
  • Experience editing content from a variety of sources, including product footage, lifestyle shoots, UGC, and screen recordings.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects, with moderate experience in 2D motion graphics.
  • Strong understanding of pacing, visual storytelling, composition, and motion design.
  • Familiarity with sound design basics, including sound effects, dialogue cleanup, music selection, and audio mixing.
  • Experience tailoring content for social media and marketplace platforms, especially short-form formats.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills in a distributed, multicultural team environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Passion for staying current with video trends, tools, and best practices.
  • Experience with product, ecommerce, or B2B video campaigns is a plus.
  • Professional working proficiency in English (written and spoken).
  • Ability and willingness to work hours that substantially overlap with 9:00 am – 5:00 pm Pacific Time.

Key Attributes:

  • High level of integrity and dedication to quality.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Strong commitment to process improvement and operational excellence

Additional Requirements:

  • Availability to work between 8 AM to 5 PM Pacific Time
  • Reliable internet access and a private remote workstation.

How to apply:

  • Please send or attach your resume to the application
    • Kindly ensure that your resume is submitted in English, as applications with resumes in other languages will not be considered.

Sunco Lighting is an online lighting retailer based in Valencia, CA. Thanks to our amazing and talented employees, today we are one of the largest online lighting retailers in the US. Job Posting Title

AI Strategist Principal

Job Description

The Principal Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategist will help lead and scale enterprise AI adoption, governance, and value realization across the organization. This role serves as a trusted advisor within Prime's AI function and works closely with business, technology, operations, clinical, legal, privacy, security, and executive leaders. The Principal AI Strategist is responsible for accelerating the adoption of AI capabilities while ensuring alignment with enterprise strategy, governance requirements, risk management practices, and business outcomes. This strategic partner will help operationalize Prime's AI strategy, support the AI Steering Committee, facilitate AI governance processes, identify opportunities for AI-enabled transformation, and drive measurable value across business capabilities.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with the VP of AI Strategy to execute Prime's multi-year AI strategy and roadmap, translating enterprise priorities into actionable plans, business cases, investment priorities, and informed recommendations based on industry, technology, vendor, and competitive trends
  • Lead Prime's AI governance framework and operating model by managing governance forums, Steering Committee processes, risk-tier evaluations, cross-functional reviews, responsible AI practices, and recommendations related to regulatory and client requirements
  • Drive enterprise AI enablement and adoption by partnering on programs, playbooks, communities of practice, champion networks, learning initiatives, and change management efforts while establishing metrics to measure utilization, adoption, and business impact
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to business and technology leaders; identify, prioritize, and advance AI-enabled transformation opportunities that align with enterprise objectives, improve workflows, promote reuse of enterprise AI assets, and deliver measurable business outcomes
  • Develop and manage AI value realization metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting, in partnership with Finance and business leaders; quantify productivity gains, operational improvements, financial benefits, and progress against enterprise targets
  • Evaluate emerging AI vendors, platforms, strategic partnerships, and market developments to support informed enterprise decisions across healthcare, PBM, and AI capabilities
  • Promote three-in-a-box collaboration across business, technology, and functional teams, and foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and responsible AI adoption
  • Other duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Science, or related area of study, or equivalent combination of education and/or relevant work experience; HS diploma from an accredited school or equivalent GED required
  • 7 years of work experience in healthcare, PBM, technology, digital transformation or analytics including 2 years of work experience developing, implementing, governing or advancing enterprise AI

Must be eligible to work in the United States without the need for work visa or residency sponsorship

Additional Qualifications

  • Understanding of AI, machine learning, generative AI, automation, and emerging digital technologies
  • Demonstrated ability to connect technology investments to measurable business outcomes
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Copilot, Azure AI, enterprise AI platforms, agentic AI solutions, and healthcare AI applications
  • Excellent executive communication and presentation skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree (MBA, MHA, MS, or related field)
  • PBM, health plan, healthcare services, or healthcare technology experience
  • Experience leading AI Centers of Excellence, innovation teams, or transformation offices
  • Experience working with executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
  • Experience with governance, risk management, and regulatory compliance

Every employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the job and, if requested, reasonable accommodations will be made to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions, absent undue hardship.
